# Background Verification for Cleaning and Facility Management Companies in India


September 29, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[1 comment](https://salarybox.in/blog/background-verification-for-cleaning-and-facility-management-companies-in-india/#comments)


Background verification for cleaning and facility management companies in India means verifying the identity of every janitor, housekeeper, deep cleaning technician, pest control operator, maintenance worker, and support staff member who enters client premises by checking their PAN and Voter ID numbers against government databases through platforms like Salarybox Verify, a process that takes under 10 minutes per worker and costs less than one hour of a cleaner’s wage, while protecting both the facility management company’s client contracts and the end clients who trust these workers with unsupervised access to their offices, hospitals, malls, residential complexes, and sensitive facilities.


India’s facility management (FM) industry is valued at over Rs 60,000 crore and growing at 15 to 20 percent annually. The industry includes integrated facility management (IFM) companies, specialized cleaning service providers, pest control companies, building maintenance firms, housekeeping service agencies, and waste management companies. These businesses collectively employ millions of workers who are deployed at client sites across corporate offices, IT parks, hospitals, shopping malls, airports, hotels, government buildings, educational institutions, residential societies, and industrial facilities.


The facility management workforce has a unique characteristic that makes verification essential: these workers have the deepest access to client premises of any outsourced workforce. A corporate office’s cleaning crew enters every room, every floor, every cabin, and every restricted area. They arrive before office hours begin and stay after employees leave. They have keys to server rooms, executive offices, document storage areas, and security control rooms. They clean boardrooms where confidential documents may be left on tables and whiteboards show strategic plans.


This level of access, combined with the fact that FM workers are almost always outsourced (deployed by the FM company, not employed by the client), creates a trust gap. The client trusts the FM company to provide verified, reliable workers. The FM company’s ability to win and retain contracts depends on that trust. When that trust is broken by a single incident involving an unverified worker, the FM company loses not just that contract but its market reputation.


## **Why Facility Management Verification Is a Contract Survival Issue**


### **FM Workers Have Master Building Access**


Cleaning and maintenance crews have access that exceeds what most employees have. A janitor cleans the CEO’s office. A maintenance technician enters the server room to fix the AC. A pest control operator sprays inside the pharmacy. A housekeeping worker enters every hotel room.


This access is granted because these tasks require it. But the access itself creates risk. A cleaning worker in a corporate office at 6 AM, before any employees arrive, has 2 hours of unsupervised access to the entire building. They can photograph documents on desks. They can access unlocked computers. They can take small items that will not be noticed immediately. They know the building’s layout, security camera positions, and alarm systems better than most employees.


If this worker operates under a false identity, the client has no accountability mechanism. PAN + Voter ID verification through[Salarybox Verify](https://salarybox.in/verify/) ensures that every worker with building access has a confirmed, traceable identity.


### **Client Contracts Mandate Verified Staff**


Enterprise clients, especially in BFSI, IT, healthcare, and government, include staff verification requirements in their FM service agreements. A typical FM contract specifies that all deployed personnel must be background-verified before site access, that verification records must be maintained and available for audit, and that the FM company is liable for any incident involving its deployed staff.


For an FM company, a single corporate client contract can be worth Rs 50 lakh to Rs 10 crore annually. Losing that contract because a cleaning worker with a fake identity stole a laptop or accessed confidential documents is a business catastrophe.


### **ISO 41001 and Quality Certifications**


Facility management companies pursuing ISO 41001 (Facility Management Systems) certification and other quality certifications must demonstrate systematic processes for personnel management, including identity verification. Verification records from Salarybox Verify provide the standardized documentation that certification auditors expect.


### **High Turnover Amplifies Risk**


FM cleaning staff turnover often exceeds 60 to 80 percent annually. A company with 1,000 deployed workers may process 700 to 800 new hires per year. Each new hire is a new identity to verify, and the pressure to fill positions (because client service levels depend on adequate staffing) creates shortcuts.


When an FM company deploys a replacement cleaner at a bank branch without verification because the previous cleaner quit that morning, the bank is now serviced by an unverified individual with after-hours access to the branch. The FM company took a shortcut to maintain service levels, and the client’s security is compromised.


### **Hospital and Healthcare Facility Access**


FM companies providing housekeeping services to hospitals have workers in operating theatres, ICUs, patient wards, pharmacies, laboratories, and biomedical waste handling areas. These workers handle biohazardous materials, work in proximity to controlled medications, and interact with vulnerable patients.


A hospital FM worker operating under a false identity who diverts controlled medications or steals patient belongings creates both security and regulatory issues. NABH accreditation reviews for hospitals include examination of outsourced staff management practices.


## **The Facility Management Verification Framework**


### **Check 1: PAN Verification (All FM Workers)**


**Why:** Confirms identity against the Income Tax Department database. Creates a verified financial identity for every deployed worker. Essential for TDS compliance and as the foundation of the worker’s identity record.


**What it reveals:** Registered name, date of birth, PAN status.


**How to do it:** Enter PAN on[Salarybox Verify](https://salarybox.in/verify/) . Result in 2 to 3 minutes. Cost: Rs 50 to Rs 200.


### **Check 2: Voter ID Verification (All FM Workers)**


**Why:** Cross-confirms identity through the Election Commission database. FM workers are predominantly from lower-income backgrounds where borrowed or shared identity documents are more common. The dual-database check catches these discrepancies.


**What it reveals:** Registered name, age or date of birth, father’s or husband’s name.


**Cross-record analysis:** Salarybox Verify compares PAN and Voter ID results automatically. Mismatches are flagged for review before the worker is deployed to any client site.


**How to do it:** Enter Voter ID in the same session. Result in 2 to 3 minutes. Cost: Rs 50 to Rs 200 additional.


### **Check 3: DL Verification (Drivers and Transport Staff)**


**Why:** FM companies often provide transport services (staff transport buses, facility inspection vehicles, waste collection vehicles). Every driver needs a valid DL.


**Who needs this:** Staff transport bus drivers, facility inspection vehicle operators, waste collection truck drivers, and any FM worker who operates a motorized vehicle as part of their duties.


**How to do it:** Enter DL number and DOB on Salarybox Verify. Result in 2 to 5 minutes. Cost: Rs 50 to Rs 200 additional.


### **Check 4: UAN Employment History (Supervisors and Managers)**


**Why:** FM supervisors and site managers are hired based on claimed experience managing cleaning operations at corporate offices, hospitals, or large facilities. Fabricated experience leads to poor service quality, client complaints, and contract losses.


**Who needs this:** Site supervisors, area managers, operations managers, and any role where salary exceeds Rs 20,000 per month based on claimed experience.


**How to do it:** Enter UAN on Salarybox Verify. Result in 5 to 30 minutes. Cost: Rs 200 to Rs 500.


## **FM Industry Scenarios**


### **Scenario 1: Laptop Theft from a Corporate Office**


An FM company deploys cleaning staff at a mid-size IT company’s office in Pune. The cleaning crew arrives at 6 AM, 2 hours before employees. Over 3 months, three laptops go missing from different floors. CCTV shows the cleaning is done normally, but the cameras do not cover every desk area. When the FM company checks worker records after the third theft, one cleaner’s PAN belongs to a person in another state. The cleaner joined 4 months ago, has knowledge of camera blind spots, and has been systematically stealing laptops during early morning shifts.


The FM company faces Rs 3.6 lakh in laptop replacement costs (charged by the client), a formal breach notice, and potential contract termination.


PAN + Voter ID verification through Salarybox Verify would have flagged the identity mismatch before the cleaner received building access cards.


### **Scenario 2: Document Photographing at a Bank Branch**


An FM company provides after-hours cleaning for 20 branches of a private bank. A cleaning worker at one branch photographs customer documents left on desks (loan applications, KYC forms with Aadhaar, PAN, and address details). The photographs are sold to a data broker. The breach is discovered when multiple customers from that branch report targeted phishing calls.


The bank terminates the FM contract (worth Rs 1.2 crore annually). The FM company faces potential legal action under DPDP Act 2023. The cleaning worker, who used a fake Voter ID, cannot be traced.


### **Scenario 3: Hospital Housekeeping Theft**


An FM company providing housekeeping at a multi-speciality hospital deploys a worker who systematically steals small medical supplies and personal belongings from patient rooms. Items include stethoscopes, pulse oximeters, patients’ phones and wallets, and medications from unattended trolleys. Total losses over 5 months: Rs 2.8 lakh.


When the theft pattern is identified through inventory reconciliation and patient complaints, the worker has already resigned. The PAN on file is invalid. NABH auditors reviewing the hospital note the inadequate verification of outsourced staff.


### **Scenario 4: The FM Supervisor with No Management Experience**


An FM company hires a “Senior Operations Supervisor” at Rs 35,000 per month to manage cleaning operations across 8 corporate client sites. The supervisor claims 7 years at two national FM companies. Within 2 months, 3 of the 8 clients file quality complaints. Cleaning schedules are disorganized. Staff attendance tracking is chaotic. Chemical usage is unmonitored (resulting in floor damage at one client site). A UAN check reveals 10 months at one small local cleaning company as a team member.


Cost: Rs 70,000 in overpaid salary, Rs 1.5 lakh in floor repair at the damaged client site, and 3 client contracts at risk.


## **Verification Across FM Business Types**


### **Integrated Facility Management Companies**


**All deployed staff:** PAN + Voter ID before deployment to any client site. This includes cleaners, housekeepers, pantry staff, security guards, electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians, and general maintenance workers.


**Site supervisors:** Add UAN verification.


**Transport and vehicle staff:** Add DL verification.


**Contract/agency workers:** Many FM companies sub-contract portions of their work. Require sub-contractors to provide worker document numbers. Run independent verification through[Salarybox Verify](https://salarybox.in/verify/) .


**Annual cost for a 2,000-worker IFM company (with 70 percent turnover = 3,400 verifications):** Rs 340,000 to Rs 1,360,000 (Rs 3.4 to Rs 13.6 lakh). For an IFM company billing Rs 50 to Rs 200 crore annually, this is 0.07 to 0.27 percent of revenue.


### **Specialized Cleaning Companies**


**Deep cleaning crews:** PAN + Voter ID. Deep cleaning teams work in empty offices, homes, and facilities with full access to all areas.


**Residential cleaning staff:** PAN + Voter ID. Workers entering private homes require verified identities (same principle as domestic help verification).


**Post-construction cleaning teams:** PAN + Voter ID. These teams access newly constructed buildings before occupants move in.


**Annual cost for a 200-worker cleaning company:** Rs 40,000 to Rs 160,000.


### **Pest Control Companies**


**All pest control technicians:** PAN + Voter ID. Pest control operators enter kitchens, food storage areas, server rooms, pharmaceutical facilities, and other sensitive areas. They handle chemicals that require responsible usage.


**DL for technicians who drive:** Add DL verification.


**Annual cost for a 50-person pest control company:** Rs 10,000 to Rs 40,000.


### **Building Maintenance and Technical Services**


**Electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians:** PAN + Voter ID. These technicians access restricted areas (electrical panels, server rooms, building management systems, rooftops) as part of their work.


**Annual cost for a 100-person maintenance company:** Rs 20,000 to Rs 80,000.


## **Building an FM Verification Policy**


### **Deployment Gate**


No worker is deployed to any client site until PAN + Voter ID verification is completed through Salarybox Verify. This is a zero-exception policy. The urgency of filling a position at a client site does not override the verification requirement.


### **Verification Timing**


Complete verification within 48 hours of hiring. For urgent replacements (worker quit, client needs coverage tomorrow), run verification on Salarybox Verify the same day (takes 10 minutes) and deploy only after verification passes.


### **Client-Specific Verification Portfolios**


Maintain a verification file for each client site showing every deployed worker’s PAN and Voter ID verification results. When workers are rotated between sites, update the site-specific files. When a client audit requests verification records, the documentation should be available within 24 hours.


### **Worker Rotation Verification**


When workers are transferred between client sites, verify that their records are current (within 6 months). For workers being deployed to high-security sites (banks, data centres, government facilities) after working at lower-security sites, re-verify before the new deployment.


### **Sub-Contractor Worker Verification**


FM companies that sub-contract work to smaller firms must extend verification requirements to sub-contractor workers. Require sub-contractors to submit worker document numbers before deployment. Run independent verification. Sub-contractor workers have the same access as directly employed workers and need the same verification.


### **Incident Protocol**


When a security incident (theft, data breach, property damage) occurs at a client site, the first step is to verify the deployed workers’ verification records. If all workers were verified, the FM company demonstrates due diligence. If any worker was unverified, this becomes a separate compliance issue that weakens the FM company’s position.


## **Cost Analysis: FM Verification**


### **Cost of Verification**


PAN + Voter ID per worker: Rs 100 to Rs 400. DL per driver: Rs 50 to Rs 200 additional. UAN per supervisor: Rs 200 to Rs 500 additional.


### **Cost of Not Verifying**


One laptop theft at a corporate client: Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh per device + contract risk. One data breach at a bank branch: Contract termination + legal liability. One hospital incident involving unverified housekeeping: NABH audit findings + contract loss. One client contract lost due to verification gap: Rs 10 lakh to Rs 10 crore annually. Reputation damage from a publicized incident: Loss of multiple client contracts.


### **The Business Case**


For an FM company with 1,000 workers spending Rs 3 lakh annually on verification, the cost per worker is Rs 300. The annual billing per worker is Rs 1.5 to Rs 3 lakh. The verification cost is 0.1 to 0.2 percent of billing. One prevented incident saves more than the entire annual verification budget. One retained client contract because of demonstrated verification pays for verification across the entire company.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Should facility management companies verify all cleaning staff?**


Yes. Every cleaning worker enters client premises, often with unsupervised after-hours access. PAN + Voter ID verification through[Salarybox Verify](https://salarybox.in/verify/) takes 10 minutes per worker and costs Rs 100 to Rs 400. For a company deploying 500 workers, annual verification cost (including turnover) is Rs 150,000 to Rs 600,000.


### **How do I verify workers quickly for urgent client deployments?**


Collect PAN and Voter ID numbers during the hiring interview. Run verification on Salarybox Verify immediately (takes 5 to 10 minutes). Issue deployment orders only after verification passes. Even for same-day replacements, the 10-minute verification window is achievable without delaying deployment.


### **Do enterprise clients require FM staff verification?**


Yes. BFSI, IT, healthcare, and government clients increasingly include verification requirements in FM service agreements. Companies that can demonstrate systematic verification through government database checks win contracts over those that cannot. PDF reports from Salarybox Verify provide audit-ready documentation.


### **How does verification help retain FM clients?**


Clients switch FM providers for two reasons: poor service quality and security concerns. Verified staff address the security concern directly. Including “all deployed staff verified through government databases” in proposals and client reviews differentiates your company. When a competitor’s unverified worker causes an incident at a client they share, your verified workforce becomes your strongest retention argument.


### **How much does FM worker verification cost?**


PAN + Voter ID costs Rs 100 to Rs 400 per worker on Salarybox Verify. No subscription, no contract, no minimum volume. For a 300-worker FM company with 60 percent turnover (480 verifications annually), the cost is Rs 48,000 to Rs 192,000. Less than one month’s billing from most client contracts.


### **What verification do hospital housekeeping staff need?**


PAN + Voter ID at minimum. Hospital housekeeping workers access patient rooms, operating theatres, pharmacies, and laboratories. Their identity must be confirmed against two government databases before hospital access is granted. For workers handling biomedical waste or working near controlled medication areas, verified identity is both a security and regulatory requirement.


### **What records should FM companies maintain?**


For each worker: PAN verification report (PDF from Salarybox Verify), Voter ID verification report (PDF), client site deployment history, verification date, and consent form. Maintain client-specific verification portfolios. Keep records for the duration of deployment plus one year. These records support client audits, insurance claims, incident investigations, and ISO certification reviews.

Facility management workers have more access to your building than your own employees. They enter every room, every floor, every restricted area. They work when nobody else is watching. They know your building’s layout better than your security team. And they should have verified identities, confirmed against government databases, before they receive a single key.
